005package org.wpilib.command3.sysid;
006
007import static org.wpilib.units.Units.Second;
008import static org.wpilib.units.Units.Seconds;
009import static org.wpilib.units.Units.Volts;
010import static org.wpilib.util.ErrorMessages.requireNonNullParam;
011
012import java.util.function.Consumer;
013import org.wpilib.command3.Command;
014import org.wpilib.command3.Mechanism;
015import org.wpilib.sysid.SysIdRoutineLog;
016import org.wpilib.system.Timer;
017import org.wpilib.units.VoltageUnit;
018import org.wpilib.units.measure.Time;
019import org.wpilib.units.measure.Velocity;
020import org.wpilib.units.measure.Voltage;
021
022/**
023 * A SysId characterization routine for a single mechanism. Mechanisms may have multiple motors.
024 *
025 * <p>A single subsystem may have multiple mechanisms, but mechanisms should not share test
026 * routines. Each complete test of a mechanism should have its own SysIdRoutine instance, since the
027 * log name of the recorded data is determined by the mechanism name.
028 *
029 * <p>The test state (e.g. "quasistatic-forward") is logged once per iteration during test
030 * execution, and once with state "none" when a test ends. Motor frames are logged every iteration
031 * during test execution.
032 *
033 * <p>Timestamps are not coordinated across data, so motor frames and test state tags may be
034 * recorded on different log frames. Because frame alignment is not guaranteed, SysId parses the log
035 * by using the test state flag to determine the timestamp range for each section of the test, and
036 * then extracts the motor frames within the valid timestamp ranges. If a given test was run
037 * multiple times in a single logfile, the user will need to select which of the tests to use for
038 * the fit in the analysis tool.
039 */
040public class SysIdRoutine extends SysIdRoutineLog {
041  private final Config m_config;
042  private final SysIdMechanism m_mechanism;
043  private final Consumer<State> m_recordState;
044
045  /**
046   * Create a new SysId characterization routine.
047   *
048   * @param config Hardware-independent parameters for the SysId routine.
049   * @param mechanism Hardware interface for the SysId routine.
050   */
051  public SysIdRoutine(Config config, SysIdMechanism mechanism) {
052    super(mechanism.name);
053    m_config = config;
054    m_mechanism = mechanism;
055    m_recordState = config.recordState != null ? config.recordState : this::recordState;
056  }
057
058  /** Hardware-independent configuration for a SysId test routine. */
059  public static class Config {
060    /** The voltage ramp rate used for quasistatic test routines. */
061    public final Velocity<VoltageUnit> rampRate;
062
063    /** The step voltage output used for dynamic test routines. */
064    public final Voltage stepVoltage;
065
066    /** Safety timeout for the test routine commands. */
067    public final Time timeout;
068
069    /** Optional handle for recording test state in a third-party logging solution. */
070    public final Consumer<State> recordState;
071
072    /** Default voltage ramp rate used in quasistatic test routines, set to 1 volt per second. */
073    public static final Velocity<VoltageUnit> DEFAULT_RAMP_RATE = Volts.of(1).per(Second);
074
075    /** Default step voltage used in dynamic test routines, set to 7 volts. */
076    public static final Voltage DEFAULT_STEP_VOLTAGE = Volts.of(7);
077
078    /** Default timeout used to automatically end test routine commands, set to 10 seconds. */
079    public static final Time DEFAULT_TIMEOUT = Seconds.of(10);
080
081    /**
082     * Create a new configuration for a SysId test routine. To use the default config values, pass
083     * in the provided static default fields.
084     *
085     * @param rampRate The voltage ramp rate used for quasistatic test routines.
086     * @param stepVoltage The step voltage output used for dynamic test routines.
087     * @param timeout Safety timeout for the test routine commands.
088     * @param recordState Optional handle for recording test state in a third-party logging
089     *     solution. If provided, the test routine state will be passed to this callback instead of
090     *     logged in WPILog.
091     */
092    public Config(
093        Velocity<VoltageUnit> rampRate,
094        Voltage stepVoltage,
095        Time timeout,
096        Consumer<State> recordState) {
097      requireNonNullParam(rampRate, "rampRate", "SysIdRoutine.Config");
098      requireNonNullParam(stepVoltage, "stepVoltage", "SysIdRoutine.Config");
099      requireNonNullParam(timeout, "timeout", "SysIdRoutine.Config");
100      this.rampRate = rampRate;
101      this.stepVoltage = stepVoltage;
102      this.timeout = timeout;
103      this.recordState = recordState;
104    }
105
106    /**
107     * Create a new configuration for a SysId test routine.
108     *
109     * @param rampRate The voltage ramp rate used for quasistatic test routines.
110     * @param stepVoltage The step voltage output used for dynamic test routines.
111     * @param timeout Safety timeout for the test routine commands.
112     * @return A Config object with the specified ramp rate, step voltage, and timeout that records
113     *     to a DataLog file.
114     */
115    public static Config useDataLog(
116        Velocity<VoltageUnit> rampRate, Voltage stepVoltage, Time timeout) {
117      return new Config(rampRate, stepVoltage, timeout, null);
118    }
119
120    /**
121     * Create a default configuration for a SysId test routine with all default settings.
122     *
123     * <p>rampRate: 1 volt/sec
124     *
125     * <p>stepVoltage: 7 volts
126     *
127     * <p>timeout: 10 seconds
128     *
129     * @return A Config object with the default ramp rate, step voltage, and timeout that records to
130     *     a DataLog file.
131     */
132    public static Config defaults() {
133      return new Config(DEFAULT_RAMP_RATE, DEFAULT_STEP_VOLTAGE, DEFAULT_TIMEOUT, null);
134    }
135  }
136
137  /**
138   * A mechanism to be characterized by a SysId routine. Defines callbacks needed for the SysId test
139   * routine to control and record data from the mechanism.
140   */
141  public static class SysIdMechanism {
142    /** Sends the SysId-specified drive signal to the mechanism motors during test routines. */
143    public final Consumer<? super Voltage> drive;
144
145    /**
146     * Returns measured data (voltages, positions, velocities) of the mechanism motors during test
147     * routines.
148     */
149    public final Consumer<SysIdRoutineLog> log;
150
151    /** The mechanism containing the motor(s) that is (or are) being characterized. */
152    public final Mechanism mechanism;
153
154    /** The name of the mechanism being tested. */
155    public final String name;
156
157    /**
158     * Create a new mechanism specification for a SysId routine.
159     *
160     * @param drive Sends the SysId-specified drive signal to the mechanism motors during test
161     *     routines.
162     * @param log Returns measured data of the mechanism motors during test routines. To return
163     *     data, call `motor(string motorName)` on the supplied `SysIdRoutineLog` instance, and then
164     *     call one or more of the chainable logging handles (e.g. `voltage`) on the returned
165     *     `MotorLog`. Multiple motors can be logged in a single callback by calling `motor`
166     *     multiple times.
167     * @param mechanism The mechanism containing the motor(s) that is (or are) being characterized.
168     *     Will be declared as a requirement for the returned test commands.
169     * @param name The name of the mechanism being tested. Will be appended to the log entry title
170     *     for the routine's test state, e.g. "sysid-test-state-mechanism". Defaults to the name of
171     *     the mechanism if left null.
172     */
173    public SysIdMechanism(
174        Consumer<Voltage> drive, Consumer<SysIdRoutineLog> log, Mechanism mechanism, String name) {
175      this.drive = drive;
176      this.log = log != null ? log : _ -> {};
177      this.mechanism = mechanism;
178      this.name = name != null ? name : mechanism.getName();
179    }
180
181    /**
182     * Create a new mechanism specification for a SysId routine. The name of the routine is
183     * generated based on the name of the given mechanism.
184     *
185     * @param drive Sends the SysId-specified drive signal to the mechanism motors during test
186     *     routines.
187     * @param log Returns measured data of the mechanism motors during test routines. To return
188     *     data, call `motor(string motorName)` on the supplied `SysIdRoutineLog` instance, and then
189     *     call one or more of the chainable logging handles (e.g. `voltage`) on the returned
190     *     `MotorLog`. Multiple motors can be logged in a single callback by calling `motor`
191     *     multiple times.
192     * @param mechanism The mechanism containing the motor(s) that is (or are) being characterized.
193     *     Will be declared as a requirement for the returned test commands. The mechanism's `name`
194     *     will be appended to the log entry title for the routine's test state, e.g.
195     *     "sysid-test-state-mechanism".
196     */
197    public SysIdMechanism(
198        Consumer<Voltage> drive, Consumer<SysIdRoutineLog> log, Mechanism mechanism) {
199      this(drive, log, mechanism, null);
200    }
201  }
202
203  /** Motor direction for a SysId test. */
204  public enum Direction {
205    /** Forward. */
206    FORWARD,
207    /** Reverse. */
208    REVERSE
209  }
210
211  /**
212   * Returns a command to run a quasistatic test in the specified direction.
213   *
214   * <p>The command will call the `drive` and `log` callbacks supplied at routine construction once
215   * per iteration. Upon command end or interruption, the `drive` callback is called with a value of
216   * 0 volts.
217   *
218   * @param direction The direction in which to run the test.
219   * @return A command to run the test.
220   */
221  public Command quasistatic(Direction direction) {
222    double outputSign =
223        switch (direction) {
224          case FORWARD -> 1.0;
225          case REVERSE -> -1.0;
226        };
227    State state =
228        switch (direction) {
229          case FORWARD -> State.QUASISTATIC_FORWARD;
230          case REVERSE -> State.QUASISTATIC_REVERSE;
231        };
232
233    return m_mechanism
234        .mechanism
235        .run(
236            co -> {
237              Timer timer = Timer.createStarted();
238              while (!timer.hasElapsed(m_config.timeout)) {
239                m_mechanism.drive.accept(
240                    (Voltage) m_config.rampRate.times(Seconds.of(timer.get() * outputSign)));
241                m_mechanism.log.accept(this);
242                m_recordState.accept(state);
243                co.yield();
244              }
245            })
246        .whenExited(this::stopRoutine)
247        .named("sysid-" + state + "-" + m_mechanism.name);
248  }
249
250  /**
251   * Returns a command to run a dynamic test in the specified direction.
252   *
253   * <p>The command will call the `drive` and `log` callbacks supplied at routine construction once
254   * per iteration. Upon command end or interruption, the `drive` callback is called with a value of
255   * 0 volts.
256   *
257   * @param direction The direction in which to run the test.
258   * @return A command to run the test.
259   */
260  public Command dynamic(Direction direction) {
261    double outputSign =
262        switch (direction) {
263          case FORWARD -> 1.0;
264          case REVERSE -> -1.0;
265        };
266    State state =
267        switch (direction) {
268          case FORWARD -> State.DYNAMIC_FORWARD;
269          case REVERSE -> State.DYNAMIC_REVERSE;
270        };
271
272    return m_mechanism
273        .mechanism
274        .run(
275            co -> {
276              Voltage output = m_config.stepVoltage.times(outputSign);
277              Timer timer = Timer.createStarted();
278              while (!timer.hasElapsed(m_config.timeout)) {
279                m_mechanism.drive.accept(output);
280                m_mechanism.log.accept(this);
281                m_recordState.accept(state);
282                co.yield();
283              }
284            })
285        .whenExited(this::stopRoutine)
286        .named("sysid-" + state + "-" + m_mechanism.name);
287  }
288
289  private void stopRoutine() {
290    m_mechanism.drive.accept(Volts.of(0));
291    m_recordState.accept(State.NONE);
292  }
293}
